Hey Simon —

Quick answers to your questions: 

1) Burst behavior: The burst window is additive capacity that allows 3x your baseline commit for short intervals. It is controlled by a token-bucket algorithm so short spikes are absorbed. For multi-hour sustained surges (e.g., 3 hours at 2x), the system will start draining the burst bucket and then revert to soft-throttling (queueing and 429s depending on route). We can provision a temporary higher burst window for campaign periods — we typically recommend a scheduled temporary boost (24–72 hours) which we can enable once we have the signed order.

2) Route-level limits: The baseline commit change does not automatically change per-route configured qps limits. We can lift the /generate route limit from 800 req/s to 1,200 req/s as part of the rollout; that change is reversible and can be staged over a few hours.

3) Security: Redwood stores customer data encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS1.3). We maintain SOC 2 Type II and will attach the latest attestation. See the security appendix for the specific page references.

I've attached a short throughput-matrix.pdf that maps expected p50/p95 latency at different commit and qps combinations based on your current model and sequences.

If you want a 30-min run-through, I'm available Tue/Wed this week.

Cheers,

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: throughput-matrix.pdf]
